title: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: A Guide for Australian Workers
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, Medicare levy, super guarantee, and award rates. Estimate your take-home pay.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare, and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: Does casual loading affect my annual salary calculation?
faqs.a: Yes. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate under most awards. To calculate annual salary as a casual, first add the 25% loading to your base rate, then multiply by your weekly hours and 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour; with casual loading it becomes $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How is tax and the Medicare levy applied to my annual salary?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% on amounts above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income, though low-income thresholds may reduce or remove it. These are applied to your annual salary after any deductions.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

Understanding your **hourly rate to annual salary** is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and planning your tax. The basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees working a standard 38-hour week, the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This gives you your total earnings before any deductions. For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual salary would be $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If you work a different number of hours each week, substitute your actual weekly hours into the formula.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the same example: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140 per week, so $2,280 per fortnight. This can help you match your budget to your pay cycle.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour** for a 38-hour week, equating to **$1,004.90 per week. Casual employees receive a 25% casual loading on top, making the casual rate **$33.05 per week**. These are minimums; many awards and enterprise agreements pay higher rates. If you are covered by an award, check your specific classification. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on your base hourly rate. When you use the [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add casual loading automatically. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – always enter the base rate and let the tool add the loading. Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is **12%** for 2026–27, up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830**. So if your annual salary is $60,000, your employer must contribute an additional $7,200 into your super fund.

### Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross salary, the Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates. For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax brackets are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, the **Medicare levy** is generally 2% of your taxable income. Low-income earners may be eligible for a reduction or exemption based on thresholds from the 2025–26 year (as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide). For a single person, the levy-free threshold is approximately $24,276, with a gradual phase-in up to $30,345. If you earn above that, you pay the full 2%.

To estimate your take-home pay after tax and Medicare, use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page. Remember that this estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Using Average Earnings as a Benchmark

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were **$2,083.70 per week**, and all employees (including part-time) averaged **$1,579.20 per week**. These are averages across the workforce, not medians for any specific job. If you see an industry or state average, treat it as a general guide, not a precise figure for your role. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context.

### Important Disclaimer

This conversion assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed calculations, visit the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page or the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page. If you need to check award-specific rates, see the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).
